overview: This Senate resolution honors the Americans killed by Hamas and allied groups in and after the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel, which killed more than 1,200 people and led to 251 people, including 12 Americans, being taken hostage in Gaza. It lists by name Americans who were killed, notes that the State Department has confirmed at least 46 American deaths, and recognizes the Americans later released through diplomatic efforts under successive U.S. administrations. The resolution condemns Hamas, expresses condolences to victims' families, and urges the U.S. government to keep using diplomatic and legal tools on behalf of Americans held hostage anywhere. It also notes that families have sued in U.S. courts those accused of supporting Hamas, and it sends a copy to the Secretary of State to share with the families. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution formally honors American victims, recognizes the families' ongoing search for accountability, and affirms that the United States will keep working for Americans taken hostage abroad.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding, and it creates no new legal remedies for victims' families.
